subject: Decision Making
subcategory: Famous Decisions That Changed the World
title: Kodak Ignores Digital
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Kodak Ignores Digital.

hook.text: A Kodak engineer invented the digital camera in 1975. Kodak shelved it because it threatened their film business.

buildup.text: Kodak dominated photography for a century. Film and processing generated enormous profits. Why disrupt yourself?

discovery.text: By 2000, digital cameras exploded. Kodak scrambled to adapt but was decades behind companies that embraced digital.

twist.text: Kodak filed for bankruptcy in 2012. The company that invented digital photography was destroyed by digital photography.

climax.text: Kodak's choice to protect profits over pursuing innovation is the classic innovator's dilemma.

punchline.text: Invented digital, killed by digital. Protecting today destroyed tomorrow.

quiz.question: What is the innovator's dilemma that Kodak fell into?
options: Protecting current profits by suppressing innovations that would disrupt them
